Map it out in terms of user interface.

What your program does is run forever, unless the user selects the exit option, meaning most of the logic will be in a while loop which will keep on running until intentionally broken (user chooses "exit" option -> your code breaks the loop).

The code inside any loop will keep repeating until the condition of the loop no longer holds true, meaning the code inside this loop will represent 1 entire workflow from beginning to end, and then it'll go back to the start once the code inside the loop has reached its end.

The code inside the while loop should print out instructions that tell the user what actions can be done, like

(a) Add job

(b) Exit

(I didn't read the problem very attentively, there could be more/less options needed, you figure it out)

...after which you need to write write a line of code to request user input (probably using cin but there are other ways, use whatever you learned). The loop will pause at this point, until the user types something in and hits enter.

Once an input comes in, determine if the user typed a or b or something invalid. If it's a, write code that asks for further inputs in the same way, either by offering options (a,b,c...) or asking the user to type something, e.g. "input the job name." If it's b (exit) then just break the loop (you can use the break keyword to end the loop or explicitly exit the entire program). If the input is invalid, ask the same question again (if only we knew of a structure that allowed things to be repeated indefinitely....... -> you can do loops inside loops).
